data.value: Notices a part that vanished or moved and new material on the bed. Does not notice the quality of the first layer, problems at the nozzle or defects inside the part.
data.comment: T-154: what the detector 'bed-change' detects and what not (from the T-152 spike).

data.name: DetectorBedChangeLimitation
data.value: Known limitation: less reliable with dark filament on a black sheet.
data.comment: T-154: known limitation of 'bed-change', shown marked under its description (T-163 may fix it later).

data.name: DetectorAirPrinting
data.comment: T-167: name of the detector 'air-printing' in the settings and the notification (user decision 2026-11-04: Czech 'Tisk do vzduchu').

data.name: DetectorAirPrintingDescription
data.value: Notices that the printer goes on printing (the Z axis rises) but nothing grows on the bed any more, e.g. filament that ran out unnoticed, a slipping extruder or a clogged nozzle. Only for printers whose bed moves down while printing (Core One, XL). Does not notice thinner walls, the surface quality or one of several parts that stops growing.
data.comment: T-167: what the detector 'air-printing' detects and what not; it is offered only for printers whose bed moves down in Z (Core One, XL).

data.name: DetectorAirPrintingLimitation
data.value: Known limitation: reports the failure only after the Z axis rose another ~3 mm (minutes, half an hour and more on slow prints). Does not judge parts mostly hidden under the head, the first ~6 mm after the start or after the camera reconnects, and a wipe tower that keeps growing can hide the failure. A part with a wider lower step that ends, or several parts of which most end earlier, can raise a false alarm.
data.comment: T-167: known limitations of 'air-printing', shown marked under its description (alarm delay in mm of Z, small parts under the head, the start, the wipe tower, false alarms when most of the print ends early; user decision 2026-11-05).
